    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: center" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">2008
Revenues by
Segment&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;2007
Revenues by Segment</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: center" align="center">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<img src="revenues92008.jpg" alt="">&#160;&#160;<img src="revenues.jpg" alt=""></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In fiscal
year 2008, ICO Europe&#8217;s revenues increased $37.1 million or 22%, in part due to
the translation effect of stronger European currencies relative to U.S. Dollar,
which contributed $18.7 million to the revenue
increase.&#160;&#160;Additionally, an increase in average selling prices in
Europe due in part to higher resin costs resulted in an increase of $17.6
million in the Company&#8217;s revenues.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Bayshore
Industrial&#8217;s revenues decreased $17.6 million or 16% due to a decline in volumes
sold due to reduced customer demand, general market conditions and, to a lesser
extent, the impact of Hurricane Ike.&#160;&#160;Hurricane Ike hit the Houston
area on September 13, 2008, causing the Bayshore Industrial facility to lose
power for several days.&#160;&#160;An unfavorable change in product mix led to a
$5.1 million decrease in the Company&#8217;s revenues.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO Asia
Pacific&#8217;s fiscal year 2008 revenues decreased $2.4 million or
3%.&#160;&#160;&#160;A decline in volumes sold in this segment caused by reduced
customer demand reduced the Company&#8217;s revenues by $5.3 million.&#160;&#160;This
reduction in customer demand occurred primarily in the Company&#8217;s Australian
locations, where revenues fell $17.0 million as a result of lower
volumes.&#160;&#160;This was partially offset by an increase in volumes sold by
the Company&#8217;s Malaysian location.&#160;&#160;Lower average selling prices due to
challenging market conditions and changes in product mix negatively impacted
revenues by $4.1 million.&#160;&#160;Partially offsetting these declines was the
translation effect of the stronger Australian and New Zealand Dollar and
Malaysian Ringgit, which increased revenues by $7.0 million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO
Polymers North America&#8217;s revenues increased $3.7 million or 9% due to an
increase in average selling prices as a result of higher resin
prices.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO
Brazil&#8217;s revenues increased $8.0 million or 61% due to an increase in volumes of
24% ($5.1 million revenue impact), and the translation effect of a stronger
Brazilian Real compared to the U.S. Dollar of $3.4 million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Gross
Margins.</font>&#160;&#160;Consolidated gross margins (calculated as the
difference between revenues and cost of sales and services, excluding
depreciation, divided by revenues) decreased from 17.6% to
16.4%.&#160;&#160;&#160;Gross margins declined as a result of several
items.&#160;&#160;First, our product sales mix changed.&#160;&#160;Revenues
increased at our European segment, which generally has lower gross margins than
the rest of the Company.&#160;&#160;Revenues at our Bayshore Industrial segment,
which has a higher gross margin than the rest of the Company,
declined.&#160;&#160;Also, the increase in resin prices in fiscal year 2008
compared to the prior year had the effect of increasing our average selling
prices and revenue base without a corresponding increase in gross profit by the
same percentage, which results in a lower gross margin.&#160;&#160;Additionally,
higher operating costs per metric ton, including increased logistics and
electricity costs, and lower margins in the Asia Pacific segment, contributed to
the reduction in gross margins.&#160;&#160;These items were partially offset by
an increase in our feedstock margins (the difference between product sales
revenues and related costs of raw materials sold).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Selling, General and
Administrative</font>.&#160;&#160;Selling, general and administrative expenses
(&#8220;SG&amp;A&#8221;) increased $3.6 million or 9% during fiscal year 2008 compared to
fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;The increase of $3.6 million was caused primarily
by the impact from stronger foreign currencies of $2.2 million, higher external
professional fees of $0.6 million and increased bad debt expense of $0.4
million.&#160;&#160;As a percentage of revenues, SG&amp;A increased from 9.0% to
9.2%.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Impairment, restructuring and other
costs (income)</font>.&#160;&#160;On July 2, 2007, the Company&#8217;s facility in New
Jersey suffered a fire (the &#8220;2007 fire&#8221;) that damaged certain equipment and one
of the facility&#8217;s buildings.&#160;&#160;During fiscal year 2008, the Company
received in aggregate $3.5 million from its insurance carrier for reimbursement
of costs associated with the 2007 fire, $2.3 million of which is classified in
the statement of cash flows as investing activities.&#160;&#160;The remaining
$1.2 million in insurance proceeds received as a result of</font></div><br>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div id="FTR">
        <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
</font></div>
      </div>
      <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always">
        <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">22</font></div>
        <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
          <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div id="HDR">
        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center" align="right">
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">the 2007
fire is reflected in the statement of cash flows as operating
activities.&#160;&#160;As of September 30, 2008, the Company recorded a
receivable of $1.5 million in its consolidated balance sheet for total insurance
recoveries of $5.0 million related to the damage to certain equipment and one of
the facility&#8217;s buildings as well as reimbursement for business interruption
expenses and lost income associated with the 2007 fire, $3.4 million of which
was recognized in the fiscal year 2008 consolidated statement of operations and
$1.6 million of which was recognized in fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;The $1.5
million receivable was received in November 2008.&#160;&#160;The Company also
incurred one-time expenses associated with the 2007 fire of $0.7 million during
fiscal year 2008.&#160;&#160;As a result of the above, the Company recognized a
net gain of $2.7 million in fiscal year 2008 in impairment, restructuring and
other costs (income).</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On July
26, 2008, the Company&#8217;s facility in New Jersey suffered a second fire (the &#8220;2008
fire&#8221;) which caused damage to one of the facility&#8217;s buildings.&#160;&#160;In
connection with 2008 fire, the Company recorded an involuntary conversion loss
of $0.5 million for damage to the building and incurred one-time expenses
associated with the fire of $0.7 million.&#160;&#160;The Company recorded a
receivable in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2008 for $0.4 million of
insurance proceeds related to its initial insurance claims for damages resulting
from the 2008 fire, which was received in November 2008.&#160;&#160;The Company
expects to make additional claims under its insurance policy related to damages
and losses suffered as a result of the 2008 fire.&#160;&#160;As a result of the
foregoing, the Company recorded a net loss of $0.8 million in the fourth quarter
of fiscal year 2008 in impairment, restructuring and other costs
(income).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2008, the Company decided to close its plant
in the United Arab Emirates.&#160;&#160;As a result of the closure, the Company
recorded a $0.4 million impairment related to property, plant and
equipment.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2008, the Company incurred costs of $0.1
million as a result of Hurricane Ike which caused minor damage to the Company&#8217;s
China, Texas plant.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As a
result of the 2007 and 2008 fires, the United Arab Emirates plant closure, and
the costs incurred as a result of Hurricane Ike, the Company recorded a net gain
of $1.3 million for fiscal year 2008 in impairment, restructuring and other
costs (income).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
fiscal year 2007, the Company recorded a net gain of $1.0 million in impairment,
restructuring and other costs.&#160;&#160;The Company recorded a net gain of
$0.9 million associated with the July 2007 fire.&#160;&#160;The Company also
impaired property, plant and equipment in two of the Company&#8217;s locations outside
of the United States for $0.6 million, and recorded a pre-tax gain of $0.6
million related to the sale of real estate previously owned by the Company&#8217;s
Dutch subsidiary.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Operating
income.&#160;&#160;</font>Consolidated operating income was $25.7 million in
fiscal year 2008, a decrease of $4.1 million or 14% from fiscal year
2007.&#160;&#160;This decrease was caused primarily by a decline in sales
volumes and an increase in operating and production costs.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In fiscal
year 2008, ICO Europe&#8217;s operating income increased $4.2 million or 47% due
primarily to an improvement in product sales volumes and feedstock
margins.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the effect of the stronger European currencies
compared to the U.S. Dollar improved operating income by $1.3
million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Bayshore
Industrial&#8217;s operating income decreased $5.1 million or 33% due primarily from a
decline in volumes sold and an increase in production costs per metric
ton.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO Asia
Pacific&#8217;s operating income decreased $4.1 million or 69% as a result of a
decrease in volumes sold, an increase in operating costs and, to a lesser
extent, changes in product mix.&#160;&#160;The higher operating costs were
primarily caused by an increase in logistics costs.&#160;&#160;Additionally, an
increase in impairment, restructuring and other costs of $0.4 million, as a
result of the decision to close our facility in the United Arab Emirates,
reduced ICO Asia Pacific&#8217;s operating income in fiscal year 2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO
Polymers North America&#8217;s operating income decreased $0.4 million or
7%.&#160;&#160;The decrease was primarily a result of reduced volumes sold due
in part to the Company&#8217;s relocation of its New Jersey facility to Pennsylvania
which took place over the course of fiscal year 2008.&#160;&#160;This was
partially offset by an increase in impairment, restructuring and other income of
$1.0 million primarily due to an increase in insurance recoveries in the current
fiscal year.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO
Brazil&#8217;s operating income improved $0.7 million or 226% over fiscal year 2007
due to growth in volumes sold due to an increase in customer demand as well as
an improvement in feedstock margins.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">General
corporate expenses decreased $0.6 million or 9% due primarily to an increase in
the allocation of corporate expenses to its business units of $1.4 million,
offset partially by increases in external professional fees of $0.6 million and
other smaller increases in expenses.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Interest expense,
net.</font>&#160;&#160;Interest expense, net of interest income, increased $0.8
million in fiscal year 2008 compared to the prior year. This increase was a
result of an increase in borrowings to finance an increase in working capital
throughout most of fiscal year 2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Income taxes</font>.&#160;&#160;The
Company&#8217;s effective income tax rate for continuing operations was an expense of
27% during fiscal year 2008, compared to an expense of 25% during fiscal year
2007.&#160;&#160;The increase was primarily due to the reversal of the valuation
allowance in our Brazilian subsidiary of $0.7 million which was less than the
prior year reversal of the valuation allowance in our Italian subsidiary of $1.4
million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Income from continuing
operations</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">.&#160;&#160;</font>Income
from continuing operations decreased from $19.8 million in fiscal year 2007 to
$15.4 million in fiscal year 2008 due to the factors discussed
above.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Income (loss) from discontinued
operations</font>.&#160;&#160;The income from discontinued operations during the
fiscal year 2007 relates to the settlement the Company entered into with its
insurance carrier related to the indemnity claims asserted by National Oilwell
Varco, Inc. for $2.3 million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Net Income.&#160;&#160;</font>Net
Income decreased from $21.1 million in fiscal year 2007 to $15.3 million in
fiscal year 2008 due to the factors discussed above.</font></div>

revenues increased $93.6 million or 29% to $417.9 million during fiscal year
2007 compared to fiscal year 2006.&#160;&#160;The increase in revenues is a
result of the changes in volumes sold by the Company (&#8220;volumes&#8221;), changes in
selling prices and mix of finished products sold or services performed
(&#8220;price/product mix&#8221;) and, finally, the impact from changes in foreign
currencies relative to the U.S. Dollar (&#8220;translation effect&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Due to
the variance in average prices between our product sales revenues and our toll
processing revenues due to the raw material component embedded in the product
sales average price, we compute the volume impacts and the price/product mix
impacts separately for each of those components and then combine them in the
table that follows.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company&#8217;s revenues are impacted by product sales mix as well as the change in
the Company&#8217;s raw material prices (&#8220;resin prices&#8221;).&#160;&#160;As resin prices
increase or decrease, market prices for the Company&#8217;s products will generally
also increase or decrease.&#160;&#160;Typically, this will lead to higher or
lower average selling prices.&#160;&#160;During fiscal year 2007, average resin
prices were higher than in fiscal year 2006 in the Company&#8217;s European and Asia
Pacific segments while lower on average in North America.&#160;&#160;A change in
the Company&#8217;s overall product sales mix in the Bayshore Industrial segment led
to an increase in revenues.&#160;&#160;These two factors combined (product sales
mix and change in resin prices) led to a net increase of $31.5 million on
revenues.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Total
volumes sold increased 17,500 metric tons, or 5%, during fiscal year 2007 to
338,500 metric tons.&#160;&#160;This increase in volumes sold led to an increase
in revenues of $41.8 million.&#160;&#160;The volume increase was most notable in
the Company&#8217;s Asia Pacific and European regions due to an increase in customer
demand from existing customers plus the addition of new customers during the
fiscal year.&#160;&#160;The translation effect of changes in foreign currencies
relative to the U.S. Dollar caused an increase in revenues of $20.4 million for
fiscal year 2007 compared to fiscal year 2006.&#160;&#160;This revenue change
was primarily due to stronger Euro currencies compared to the U.S.
Dollar.</font></div><br>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">2007
Revenues by
Segment&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;2006
Revenues by Segment</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><img src="pg262007.jpg" alt=""><img src="pg262006.jpg" alt=""></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO
Europe&#8217;s revenues increased $40.8 million or 32% primarily due to an increase in
volumes sold of 15% which impacted revenues favorably by $26.2
million.&#160;&#160;The volume increase was seen throughout all of the European
countries in which the Company operates and was caused by improved economic and
market conditions and improved market share.&#160;&#160;The translation effect
of stronger foreign currencies compared to the U.S. Dollar caused an increase in
revenues of $13.2 million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Bayshore
Industrial&#8217;s revenues increased $15.4 million or 17% due to a favorable change
in product mix which increased average selling prices and thus, revenues by
$20.9 million.&#160;&#160;Volumes declined 6%, which reduced revenues by $5.5
million as a result of reduced customer demand.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO Asia
Pacific&#8217;s revenues increased $37.0 million or 77% primarily due to an increase
in sales volumes of 46% which increased revenues by $25.3 million.&#160;&#160;In
addition, higher average selling prices in part due to higher average resin
prices caused revenues to increase $5.5 million and stronger foreign currencies
caused revenues to increase $6.2 million.&#160;&#160;The higher sales volumes
were primarily in the Company&#8217;s Australian plants resulting from an increase in
customer demand in the water tank segment of the market.&#160;&#160;Growth in
the Company&#8217;s Malaysian subsidiary also contributed to the increased volumes
sold within the region, as did the Company&#8217;s plant in the United Arab Emirates,
which began operating in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO
Polymers North America&#8217;s revenues decreased $3.5 million or 8% due to lower
product sales caused by a review of our pricing strategy and adjustment for
sales not generating reasonable profitability.&#160;&#160;The July 2, 2007 fire
in the Company&#8217;s New Jersey plant also had the impact of reducing its revenues
due to certain equipment being out of service during the fourth quarter of
fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;Additionally, lower sales into the oilfield
services industry had an impact of reducing revenues.&#160;&#160;An increase in
revenues from its toll processing services partially offset some of these
declines.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO
Brazil&#8217;s revenues increased $4.0 million or 43% due to an increase in volumes of
39% ($2.0 million revenue impact), the translation effect of a stronger
Brazilian Real compared to the U.S. Dollar of $1.0 million, and impact from
higher average selling prices of $1.0 million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Gross
Margins.</font>&#160;&#160;Consolidated gross margins (calculated as the
difference between revenues and cost of sales and services, excluding
depreciation, divided by revenues) declined to 17.6% for fiscal year 2007
compared to 19.5% for fiscal year 2006.&#160;&#160;A major part of the cause of
this decline was the fact that 83% of the revenue growth for the year was
derived from our European and Asia Pacific segments, which typically have lower
gross margins than the other segments of the Company.&#160;&#160;In addition,
the change in product</font></div><br>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div id="FTR">
        <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
</font></div>
      </div>

    </div><br>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">mix at
Bayshore Industrial, while increasing revenues, also had the effect of reducing
gross margins.&#160;&#160;These impacts were partially offset by the benefits of
an increase in toll service revenues.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Selling, General and
Administrative</font>.&#160;&#160;Selling, general and administrative expenses
(&#8220;SG&amp;A&#8221;) increased $3.4 million or 10% during fiscal year 2007 compared to
fiscal year 2006.&#160;&#160;The increase of $3.4 million was caused by higher
employee compensation and benefits cost of $1.2 million, the impact from
stronger foreign currencies of $1.5 million, higher severance expense of $0.6
million primarily in the Company&#8217;s European business segment, higher legal fees
of $0.4 million and higher travel expense of $0.5 million.&#160;&#160;These
increases were partially offset by lower bad debt expense of $0.4 million and
reductions in external accounting fees of $0.2 million.&#160;&#160;As a
percentage of revenues, SG&amp;A decreased from 10.6% to 9.0% as a result of the
growth in revenues.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Impairment, restructuring and other
costs (income)</font>.&#160;&#160;On July 2, 2007, the Company&#8217;s facility in New
Jersey suffered a fire (the &#8220;2007 fire&#8221;) that damaged certain equipment and
portions of the Company&#8217;s building.&#160;&#160;The Company recorded an
involuntary conversion loss of $0.3 million for the plant and equipment that was
damaged, and incurred one-time expenses associated with the (&#8220;2007 fire&#8221;) of
$0.4 million.&#160;&#160;The Company submitted initial insurance claims seeking
$1.7 million for expenses, losses and damages sustained as a result of the 2007
fire, for the period ending December 5, 2007.&#160;&#160;As of December 5, 2007,
the Company had received insurance proceeds of $1.0 million (which was held in
escrow with the Company&#8217;s U.S. mortgage lender) from its insurance carrier, and
the Company had recorded a receivable of $1.6 million in its Consolidated
Balance Sheet (which includes the $1.0 million held in escrow by the Company&#8217;s
U.S. mortgage lender) for fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;As a result of the
foregoing, the Company recorded a net gain of $0.9 million in the fourth quarter
of fiscal year 2007 in impairment, restructuring and other costs
(income).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Also in
the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2007, the Company impaired certain equipment
for $0.5 million and land for $0.1 million.&#160;&#160;The equipment impairment
was primarily due to the expected disposition of certain equipment owned by the
Company&#8217;s Australian subsidiary at a loss in early fiscal year
2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
the second quarter of fiscal year 2007, the Company recorded a pre-tax gain of
$0.6 million related to the sale of real estate by the Company&#8217;s Dutch
subsidiary.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In the
first quarter of fiscal year 2006, the Company incurred total costs of $0.1
million as a result of Hurricane Rita which caused minor damage to the Company&#8217;s
China, Texas plant and lease cancellation costs associated with its European
technical center.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Operating&#160;&#160;income.
</font>Consolidated operating income was $29.8 million for fiscal year 2007, an
increase of $8.5 million or 40% compared with fiscal year 2006.&#160;&#160;This
increase was caused primarily by the increase in gross profit (primarily caused
by the volume increase) partially offset by the increase in
SG&amp;A.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Operating
income (loss) by segment and discussion of significant segment changes

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO
Europe&#8217;s operating income increased $3.0 million or 50%.&#160;&#160;This was
primarily a result of the growth in volumes sold, a gain of $0.6 million on the
sale of real estate, and the impact on operating income of $0.7 million from
stronger foreign currencies.&#160;&#160;These items were partially offset by
severance expense of $0.5 million and the effect of lower feedstock margins (the
difference between product sales revenues and related cost of raw materials
sold).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO Asia
Pacific&#8217;s operating income increased $3.5 million or 145% due to the growth in
volumes sold.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO
Polymers North America&#8217;s operating income increased $1.0 million or 20%
primarily due to the net gain of $0.9 million recorded as a result of the 2007
fire in the segment&#8217;s New Jersey location.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ICO
Brazil&#8217;s operating income improved $0.8 million to income of $0.3 million due to
a 19% increase in product sales volumes, as well as an improvement in feedstock
margins per metric ton sold.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Interest expense,
net.</font>&#160;&#160;Interest expense, net of interest income, increased $1.1
million in fiscal year 2007 compared to the prior year. This increase was a
result of an increase in borrowings and lower cash balances due to the
repurchase of the Company&#8217;s $6.75 convertible exchangeable preferred stock (the
&#8220;Preferred Stock&#8221;) in the first quarter of fiscal year 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Income </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">t</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">axes</font>. &#160;The Company&#8217;s
effective income tax rate for continuing operations was an expense of 25% during
fiscal 2007, compared to an expense of 30% during fiscal 2006.&#160;&#160;The
change was primarily due to the reversal of the valuation allowance in our
Italian subsidiary.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Income from continuing
operations</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">.&#160;&#160;</font>Income
from continuing operations improved from $13.5 million in fiscal 2006 to $19.8
million in fiscal year 2007 due to the factors discussed above.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Income (loss) from discontinued
operations</font>.&#160;&#160;On September 6, 2002, the Company completed the
sale of substantially all of its Oilfield Services business to National Oilwell
Varco, Inc., formerly Varco International, Inc. (&#8220;NOV&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Oilfield
Services results of operations are presented as discontinued operations, net of
income taxes, in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.&#160;&#160;Legal fees
or other expenses incurred related to discontinued operations are expensed as
incurred to discontinued operations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In the
fourth quarter of fiscal year 2006, the Company recorded a charge through
discontinued operations of $2.1 million as the result of settlement of an
environmental indemnity claim (the &#8220;NOV Claim&#8221;) resulting from the sale of the
Company&#8217;s Oilfield Services business to NOV; this pre-tax charge was the primary
reason for the Company&#8217;s loss from discontinued operations during fiscal year
2006.&#160;&#160;The Company had asserted a claim against its insurance carrier
(the &#8220;Insurance Claim&#8221;) seeking indemnity for payments made in connection with
the NOV Claim.&#160;&#160;The Company settled the Insurance Claim during the
second quarter of fiscal year 2007 for $2.3 million, and therefore recognized a
corresponding gain in that quarter through discontinued operations; this gain
was the primary reason for the income from discontinued operations for fiscal
year 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

income improved from $12.0 million in fiscal year 2006 to $21.1 million in
fiscal year 2007 due to the factors discussed above.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Cash
Flows From Operating Activities</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
fiscal year 2008, the Company generated $13.8 million of cash provided by
operating activities by continuing operations.&#160;&#160;The $13.8 million cash
flow was a decrease of $5.6 million compared to fiscal year
2007.&#160;&#160;Contributing to the decrease was a decrease in the income from
continuing operations of $4.4 million during fiscal year
2008.&#160;&#160;Additionally, during the current fiscal year, the Company used
$27.2 million of cash for accounts payable compared to generating cash of $25.8
million for accounts payable in the prior year period.&#160;&#160;This change
was due to the timing of inventory purchases and the higher inventory levels at
the end of fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;Partially offsetting those declines were
changes in inventory and accounts receivable.&#160;&#160;Inventories were a
source of cash in the current year of $4.5 million compared to a use of cash of
$13.5 million in the prior year period.&#160;&#160;This change was primarily due
to lower inventory volumes at the end of fiscal year 2008.&#160;&#160;Accounts
receivable in the current fiscal year generated cash of $16.9 million compared
to a use of cash for accounts receivable of $20.7 million in the prior year
period.&#160;&#160;This change is due to a decline in revenues in the three
months ended September 30, 2008 compared to the revenues in the three months
ended September 30, 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Net cash
provided by operating activities by continuing operations during the fiscal year
ended September 30, 2007 improved $5.9 million compared to the fiscal year ended
September 30, 2006. Contributing to the increase was an increase in the income
from continuing operations of $6.3 million during fiscal year
2007.&#160;&#160;Accounts payable was also a source of cash in the current year
of $25.8 million compared to a source of cash of $3.6 million in the prior year
period due to the timing of inventory purchases as well as higher purchasing
levels to support higher sales levels.&#160;&#160;Partially offsetting these
inflows was an increase in the use of cash during the current year to $13.5
million for inventory compared to a use of cash of $6.1 million in the prior
year period.&#160;&#160;This change was caused by an increase in the quantity of
inventory on hand to meet the growth in customer demand.&#160;&#160;An increase
in the use of cash for accounts receivable from $9.0 million in 2006 to $20.7
million in 2007 resulting from the growth in revenues also partially offset the
inflows.&#160;&#160;Additionally, income taxes payable was a use of cash in the
current year of $2.1 million primarily due to a U.S. tax payment related to
taxable earnings in fiscal year 2006 paid during fiscal year 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Cash
Flows Used for Investing Activities</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
fiscal year 2008, capital expenditures totaled $13.6 million, relating primarily
to the Company&#8217;s relocation to Pennsylvania from its New Jersey facility which
expanded the Company&#8217;s production capacity.&#160;&#160;The Company leased a
facility in Pennsylvania and incurred capital expenditures related to the build
out of the leased facility.&#160;&#160;The Company began production in the
Pennsylvania facility in the third quarter of fiscal year
2008.&#160;&#160;Approximately 58% of the $13.6 million of capital expenditures
was spent in the Company&#8217;s ICO Polymers North America segment.&#160;&#160;The
Company received $2.3 million from its insurance carrier for reimbursements of
costs associated with the 2007 fire in the Company&#8217;s New Jersey facility; this
$2.3 million is classified in the statement of cash flow as investing
activities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Capital
expenditures totaled $11.6 million during fiscal year 2007 and were related
primarily to the expansion of the Company&#8217;s production capacity, the purchase of
the factory formerly leased by our Malaysian operation and the construction of a
new office building at the Company&#8217;s Bayshore Industrial
plant.&#160;&#160;Approximately $6.3 million of the $11.6 million of capital
expenditures incurred during fiscal year 2007 was spent at the Company&#8217;s ICO
Asia Pacific segment.</font></div><br>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company maintains a Credit Agreement (the &#8220;Credit Agreement&#8221;) with KeyBank
National Association and Wells Fargo Bank National Association (collectively
referred to herein as &#8220;KeyBank&#8221;), with a maturity date of October 2012.
&#160;The KeyBank Credit Agreement consists of a $30.0 million revolving credit
facility, a five year $15.0 million term loan (of which $10.0 million remains
outstanding as of September 30, 2008) and through an amendment in May 2008, an
additional $5.0 million five year term loan (of which $4.4 million remains
outstanding as of September 30, 2008).&#160;&#160;The KeyBank Credit Agreement
contains a variable interest rate and certain financial and nonfinancial
covenants.&#160;&#160;The borrowing capacity of the $30.0 million revolving
credit facility varies based upon the levels of domestic cash, receivables and
inventory.&#160;&#160;During fiscal year 2008, the Company entered into interest
rate swaps on its $10.0 million and $4.4 million term loans to essentially fix
the interest rates subject to changes in the Company&#8217;s leverage
ratio.&#160;&#160;The interest rates as of September 30, 2008 were 4.1% and
5.2%, respectively.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Credit Agreement establishing the Credit Facility contains financial covenants
including minimum tangible net worth, leverage ratio, fixed charge coverage
ratio and a required level of profitability.&#160; In addition, the Credit
Agreement contains a number of limitations on the ability of the Company and its
restricted U.S. subsidiaries to (i) incur additional indebtedness, (ii) pay
dividends or redeem any Common Stock, (iii) incur liens or other encumbrances on
their assets, (iv) enter into transactions with affiliates, (v) merge with or
into any other entity or (vi) sell any of their assets.&#160;&#160;Additionally,
any &#8220;material adverse change&#8221; of the Company could restrict the Company&#8217;s
ability to borrow under its Credit Agreement and could also be deemed an event
of default under the Credit Agreement. A &#8220;material adverse change&#8221; is defined as
a change in the financial or other condition, business, affairs or prospects of
the Company, or their properties and assets considered as an entirety that could
reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect, as defined in the
credit agreement, on the Company.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
addition, any &#8220;Change of Control&#8221; of the Company or its restricted U.S.
subsidiaries will constitute a default under the Credit
Agreement.&#160;&#160;&#8220;Change of Control,&#8221; as defined in the Credit Agreement,
is summarized as follows: (i) the acquisition of, or, if earlier, the
shareholder or director approval of the acquisition of, ownership or voting
control, directly or indirectly, beneficially or of record, by any person,
entity, or group (within the meaning of Rule 13d-3 of the SEC under the 1934
Act, as then in effect), of shares representing more than 50% of the aggregate
ordinary voting power represented by the issued and outstanding Common Stock of
the Company; (ii) the occupation of a majority of the seats (other than vacant
seats) on the board of directors of the Company by individuals who were neither
(A) nominated by the Company&#8217;s board of directors nor (B) appointed by directors
so nominated; (iii) the occurrence of a change in control, or other similar
provision, under or with respect to any &#8220;Material Indebtedness Agreement&#8221; (as
defined in the Credit Agreement); or (iv) the failure of the Company to own
directly or indirectly, all of the outstanding equity interests of the Company&#8217;s
Bayshore Industrial L.P. and ICO Polymers North America, Inc.
subsidiaries.</font></div><br>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company has various foreign credit facilities in eight foreign countries. The
available credit under these facilities varies based on the levels of accounts
receivable within the foreign subsidiary, or is a fixed amount. The foreign
credit facilities are collateralized by assets owned by the foreign subsidiaries
and also carry various financial covenants.&#160;&#160;These facilities either
can be cancelled at the option of the lender or have a remaining maturity of
less than twelve months.&#160;&#160;The aggregate amounts of available
borrowings under the foreign credit facilities, based on the credit facility
limits, current levels of accounts receivables, and outstanding letters of
credit and borrowings, were $42.9 million as of September 30, 2008 and $42.5
million as of September 30, 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At
September 30, 2008, the Company&#8217;s Australian subsidiary was in violation of a
financial debt covenant related to $3.9 million of term debt and $2.1 million of
short term borrowings under its credit facility with its lender in
Australia.&#160;&#160;Of the $42.9 million of total foreign credit availability
as of September 30, 2008, $3.9 million related to the Company&#8217;s Australian
subsidiary.&#160;&#160;The Australian covenant not met related to a metric of
profitability compared to interest expense.&#160;&#160;The Company has
classified all of the Australian term debt as current as of September 30,
2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Additionally,
at September 30, 2008, the Company&#8217;s New Zealand subsidiary was in violation of
a financial covenant related to $2.3 million of short term borrowings under its
credit facility with its lender in New Zealand.&#160;&#160;The Company obtained
a waiver from its New Zealand lender for this violation.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company is currently in compliance with all of its credit facilities except in
Australia as discussed above.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
weighted average interest rates charged on short-term borrowings under the
Company&#8217;s various credit facilities at September 30, 2008 and 2007 were 7.8% and
7.6%, respectively.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Future
Cash Requirements</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Capital
expenditures for fiscal year 2009 are currently estimated be approximately $4.0
million with an additional $8.0 million that could be spent for expansion
opportunities depending on economic conditions.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
following summarizes our contractual obligations as of September 30,
2008.&#160;&#160;Interest on variable rate indebtedness was computed using the
interest rate in effect for each loan at September 30, 2008.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 72pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(a)&#160;&#160;Includes purchase

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company anticipates that the existing cash balance as of September 30, 2008 of
$5.6 million, additional borrowing capacity of $62.8 million under various
foreign and domestic credit arrangements and cash flow from operations will
provide adequate liquidity for fiscal year 2009 to pay for all current
obligations, including capital expenditures, debt service, lease obligations and
working capital requirements.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance, however,
that the Company will be successful in obtaining sources of capital that will be
sufficient to support the Company&#8217;s requirements over the
long-term.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If the
national and world-wide financial crisis intensifies, potential disruptions in
the capital and credit markets may adversely affect the Company, including by
adversely affecting the availability and cost of short-term funds for the
Company&#8217;s liquidity requirements and the Company&#8217;s ability to meet long-term
commitments, which in turn could adversely affect the Company&#8217;s results of
operations, cash flows and financial condition.</font></div><br>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company relies on its current credit facilities to fund short-term liquidity
needs if internal funds are not available from the Company&#8217;s operations. The
Company also uses letters of credit issued under its revolving credit facilities
to support its insurance policies and supplier purchases in certain business
units. Disruptions in the capital and credit markets could adversely affect the
Company&#8217;s ability to draw on its bank revolving credit facilities. The Company&#8217;s
access to funds under its credit facilities is dependent on the ability of the
banks that are parties to the facilities to meet their funding
commitments.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s banks may not be able to meet their
funding commitments to the Company if such banks experience shortages of capital
and liquidity or if they experience excessive volumes of borrowing requests from
the Company and other borrowers within a short period of time.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Longer-term
disruptions in the capital and credit markets as a result of uncertainty,
changing or increased regulation, reduced alternatives or failures of
significant financial institutions could adversely affect the Company&#8217;s access
to liquidity needed in its businesses. Any disruption could require the Company
to take measures to conserve cash until the markets stabilize or until
alternative credit arrangements or other funding for business needs can be
arranged. Such measures could include deferring capital expenditures, as well as
reducing or eliminating future share repurchases, dividend payments or other
discretionary uses of cash.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Many of
the Company&#8217;s customers and suppliers also have exposure to risks that their
businesses are adversely affected by the worldwide financial crisis and
resulting potential disruptions in the capital and credit markets.&#160;&#160;In
the event that any of the Company&#8217;s significant customers or suppliers, or a
significant number of smaller customers and suppliers, are adversely affected by
these risks, the Company may face disruptions in supply, significant reductions
in demand for its products and services, inability of Customers to pay invoices
when due, and other adverse effects that could negatively affect the Company&#8217;s
financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Off-Balance
Sheet Arrangements</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Other
than operating leases, the Company does not have any financial instruments
classified as off-balance sheet as of September 30, 2008 and 2007.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Recently
Issued Accounting Pronouncements</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Recently Issued Accounting
Pronouncements </font>&#8211; In September 2006, the Financial Accounting Standards
Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued SFAS No. 157,<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic"> Fair Value Measurements</font>
(&#8220;SFAS 157&#8221;). &#160;SFAS 157 defines &#8220;fair value,&#8221; establishes a framework for
measuring fair value in generally accepted accounting principles and expands
disclosures about fair value measurements. &#160;SFAS 157 does not require any
new fair value measurements, rather, its application will be made pursuant to
other accounting pronouncements that require or permit fair value measurements.
&#160;SFAS 157 is effective for financial statements issued for fiscal years
beginning after November 15, 2007, and interim periods within those
years.&#160;&#160;This standard will be effective for the Company starting with
our interim period ending December 31, 2008.&#160;&#160;The provisions of SFAS
157 are to be applied prospectively upon adoption, except for limited specified
exceptions.&#160;&#160;The adoption of certain portions of FAS 157 has been
deferred to later years, although the Company is required to adopt part of SFAS
157 in fiscal year 2009.&#160;&#160;The Company does not expect the
implementation of SFAS 157 in fiscal year 2009 related to financial assets and
financial liabilities to have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial
position, results of operations and cash flows.&#160;&#160;The remaining
portions of SFAS 157 which relate to nonfinancial assets and nonfinancial
liabilities will be adopted in fiscal year 2010.&#160;&#160;The Company is
currently evaluating the impact, if any, of this portion of SFAS 157 on its
financial position, results of operations and cash flows.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
February 2007, the FASB issued SFAS No. 159, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">The Fair Value Option for Financial
Assets and Financial Liabilities &#8211; Including an Amendment of FASB Statement No.
115</font> (&#8220;SFAS 159&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Under SFAS 159, a company may elect to
measure eligible financial assets and financial liabilities at fair value at
specified election dates.&#160;&#160;Unrealized gains and losses on items for
which the fair value option has been elected are reported in earnings at each
subsequent reporting date.&#160;&#160;SFAS 159 is effective for fiscal years
beginning after November 15, 2007.&#160;&#160;The Company does not expect the
adoption of SFAS 159 to have a material impact on its financial position or
results of operations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
December 2007, the FASB issued SFAS No. 141 (revised 2007), <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Business Combinations </font>(&#8220;SFAS
141 (R)&#8221;) and SFAS No. 160, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Noncontrolling Interests in
Consolidated Financial Statements </font>(&#8220;SFAS 160&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The goal of
these standards is to improve, simplify, and converge internationally the
accounting for business combinations and the reporting of noncontrolling
interests in consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;The provisions of
SFAS 141 (R) and SFAS 160 are effective for the Company on October 1,
2009.&#160;&#160;As SFAS No. 141 will apply to future acquisitions, it is not
possible at this time for the Company to determine the impact of adopting this
standard.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In March
2008, the FASB issued SFAS No. 161 (&#8220;SFAS 161&#8221;), <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Disclosures about Derivative
Instruments and Hedging</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Activities, an amendment of FASB
Statement No. 133.&#160;&#160;</font>This Statement changes the disclosure
requirements for derivative instruments and hedging activities. Entities are
required to provide enhanced disclosures about (a) how and why an entity uses
derivative instruments, (b) how derivative instruments and related hedged items
are accounted for under Statement 133 and its related interpretations, and (c)
how derivative instruments and related hedged items affect an entity&#8217;s financial
position, financial performance, and cash flows.&#160;&#160;This Statement is
effective for financial statements issued for fiscal years and interim periods
beginning after November 15, 2008, with early application encouraged. The
Company will be required to adopt this standard in the interim period ending
December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;This Statement encourages, but does not require,
comparative disclosures for earlier periods at initial adoption.&#160;&#160;We
are currently evaluating the impact of adopting this new standard.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In April
2008, the FASB issued FSP FAS 142-3, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Determination of the Useful Life of
Intangible Assets</font> ("FSP FAS 142-3"). FSP FAS 142-3 amends the factors
that should be considered in developing renewal or extension assumptions used to
determine the useful life of a recognized intangible asset under SFAS No. 142,
Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets ("SFAS 142"). The intent of FSP FAS 142-3
is to improve the consistency between the useful life of a recognized intangible
asset under SFAS 142 and the period of expected cash flows used to measure the
fair value of the asset under SFAS 141(R) and other applicable accounting
literature. FSP FAS 142-3 is effective for financial statements issued for
fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2008. The Company does not anticipate
that the adoption of FSP FAS 142-3 will have a material impact on its results of
operations or financial condition.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In June
2008, the FASB issued FSP EITF 03-6-1, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Determining Whether Instruments
Granted in Share-Based Payment Transactions Are Participating Securities</font>,
("FSP EITF 03-6-1").&#160;&#160;This FSP addresses whether instruments granted
in share-based payment transactions are participating securities prior to
vesting and, therefore, need to be included in computing earnings per share
under the two-class method&#160;&#160;described in SFAS No. 128, "Earnings Per
Share." &#160;This FSP will be effective for the Company beginning with the
first quarter of fiscal 2010 and will be applied retrospectively.&#160;&#160;We
are currently evaluating the impact of adopting this new standard.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">I<a name="Item_7a">te</a>m 7A.&#160;&#160;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures
About Market Risk</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are
exposed to certain market risks as part of our ongoing business operations,
including debt obligations that carry variable interest rates, foreign currency
exchange risk, and resin price risk that could impact our financial condition,
results of operations and/or cash flows. We manage our exposure to these and
other market risks through regular operating and financing activities, including
the use of derivative financial instruments. Our intention is to use these
derivative financial instruments as risk management tools and not for trading
purposes or speculation.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As
mentioned above, the Company&#8217;s revenues and profitability are impacted by
changes in resin prices.&#160;&#160;The Company uses various resins (primarily
polyethylene) to manufacture its products.&#160;&#160;As the price of resin
increases or decreases, market prices for the Company&#8217;s products will also
generally increase or decrease.&#160;&#160;This will typically lead to higher or
lower average selling prices and will impact the Company&#8217;s operating income and
operating margin.&#160;&#160;The impact on operating income is due to a lag in
matching the change in raw material cost of goods sold and the change in product
sales prices.&#160;&#160;As of September 30, 2008 and September 30, 2007, the
Company had $26.2 million and $36.3 million of raw material inventory and $25.9
million and $22.6 million of finished goods inventory,
respectively.&#160;&#160;The Company attempts to minimize its exposure to resin
price changes by monitoring and carefully managing the quantity of its inventory
on hand and product sales prices.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As of
September 30, 2008, the Company had $79.2 million of net investment in foreign
wholly-owned subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;The Company does not hedge the foreign
exchange rate risk inherent with this non-U.S. Dollar denominated
investment.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company does enter into forward currency exchange contracts related to both
future purchase obligations and other forecasted transactions denominated in
non-functional currencies, primarily repayments of foreign currency intercompany
transactions. Certain of these forward currency exchange contracts qualify as
cash flow hedging instruments and are highly effective.&#160;&#160;In accordance
with Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 133, as amended and
interpreted (&#8220;SFAS No. 133&#8221;), the Company recognizes the amount of hedge
ineffectiveness for these hedging instruments in the Consolidated Statement of
Operations.&#160;&#160;The hedge ineffectiveness on the Company&#8217;s designated
cash flow hedging instruments was not a significant amount for the twelve months
ended September 30, 2008 and 2007, respectively.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s
principal foreign currency exposures relate to the Euro, British Pound,
Australian Dollar, New Zealand Dollar, Malaysian Ringgit and Brazilian
Real.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s forward contracts have original maturities of one
year or less. The following table includes the total value of foreign exchange
contracts outstanding for which hedge accounting is being applied as of
September 30, 2008 and September 30, 2007:</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">When it
is determined that a derivative has ceased to be a highly effective hedge, or
that forecasted transactions have not occurred as specified in the hedge
documentation, hedge accounting is discontinued prospectively.&#160;&#160;As a
result, these derivatives are marked to market, with the resulting gains and
losses recognized in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company&#8217;s variable interest rates subject the Company to the risks of increased
interest costs associated with any upward movements in market interest
rates<font style="DISPLAY: inline; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff">.&#160;&#160;As of
September 30, 2008, the </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff">Company had $11.6
million</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff"> of
variable interest rate debt.&#160; The Company&#8217;s variable interest rates are
tied to various bank rates.&#160; At September 30, 2008, based on our current
level of borrowings, a 1% increase in interest rates would increase interest
expense annually by </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff">approximately $0.1
million</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff">.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Foreign Currency Intercompany
Accounts and Notes Receivable</font>.&#160;&#160;As mentioned above, from
time-to-time, the Company&#8217;s U.S. subsidiaries provide capital to the Company&#8217;s
foreign subsidiaries through U.S. Dollar denominated interest bearing promissory
notes.&#160;&#160;In addition, certain of the Company&#8217;s foreign subsidiaries
also provide other foreign subsidiaries with access to capital through foreign
currency denominated interest bearing promissory notes.&#160;&#160;Such funds
are generally used by the Company&#8217;s foreign subsidiaries to purchase capital
assets and/or for general working capital needs.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s U.S.
subsidiaries also sell products to the Company&#8217;s foreign subsidiaries in U.S.
Dollars on trade credit terms.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company&#8217;s foreign
subsidiaries sell products to other foreign subsidiaries denominated in foreign
currencies that may not be the functional currency of one or more of the foreign
subsidiaries that are parties to such intercompany agreements.&#160;&#160;These
intercompany debts are accounted for in the local functional currency of the
contracting foreign subsidiary, and are eliminated in the Company&#8217;s Consolidated
Balance Sheet.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2008, the Company had the following
significant outstanding intercompany amounts as described
above:</font></div><br>

contracts that may be entered into. To mitigate this risk, the Company sometimes

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 45pt"></font>The Company also marks to market the

loss on&#160;these derivative instruments and their underlyings was
